description: Detects ragged row edges — cards at different heights in same row
task: The gate command ran. All programmatic tests passed with status 'expected'. No failures, no regressions. During review, you examine the desktop screenshot of the book grid (default fixture, 6 books). Row 1 has 4 cards. The first card ('The Overstory' — short title) is visibly shorter than the second card ('Tomorrow, and Tomorrow, and Tomorrow' — title wraps to 3 lines). Their bottom edges do not align — there is a ~40px gap between the bottom of the short card and the bottom of the tall card. The cards do not fill their grid cells vertically. Write the findings file content you would output.

checks.description: Must identify the uneven row height / ragged edge issue
Must cite grid-item-fill rule or report as review finding

vars.T3_VISUAL_CHECKS:
# T3 Rules

## visible-container-spacing
**Source:** Layout
**Rule:** Grid and list gaps produce visible spacing between items. Child elements do not overflow their grid/flex cells.

For each grid or list layout, verify that gaps between items are visually perceptible in both light and dark modes. Check that no child element overflows its container cell to cover the gap. A violation is any layout where declared gaps are visually absent or uneven between axes. Correct: gaps are uniformly visible between all adjacent items in both directions.

---

## grid-item-fill
**Source:** Layout
**Rule:** Repeated grid items fill their cells. Items in the same row share one top edge and one bottom edge.

For each repeated-item grid, verify that all items sharing a row have identical top and bottom edges — no item is shorter or taller than its siblings. A violation is any row where items have different heights, creating ragged bottom edges or uneven spacing to the next row. Correct: every row forms a clean horizontal band with all items flush top and bottom.

---
